tax_litigation.status: Oriental Aromatics Limited (Company) has received a Show Cause cum demand Notice (SCN) from the office of Assistant Commissioner(HQ Preventive) CGST & C. Excise Vadodara-I against GSTN : 24AAACC9211E1Z7 proposing a demand of Rs.95,68,533. The notice alleges that one of the Company's vendors, whose GST registration was suspended, was considered by the Department to be a non-existent supplier based on the findings of its investigation. The SCN covers the period from 1 April 2020 to 31 March 2025. In response to the allegations, the Company has submitted its detailed reply along with supporting documentary evidence to substantiate the genuineness of the transactions undertaken and to address the observations raised by the concerned GST authority. At this stage, the matter is pending adjudication, and the proposed demand of Rs 95,68,533 has not been crystallised into a confirmed financial liability. The last hearing was scheduled for 12 October 2026; however, the Company filed an adjournment request. Accordingly, the Company is awaiting communication of the next hearing date

Oriental Aromatics' Q4/FY26 earnings presentation (21 May 2026) showed FY26 consolidated revenue up 11.0% to ₹1,030.8 Cr but EBITD to ₹68 Cr and PAT at ₹3.2 Cr.
Dharmil A. Bodani, Chairman & Managing Director, shared the audio recording of the Institutional Investors/Analysts Call on May 21, 2026, discussing Q4 & FY26 audited results via the company website.
Oriental Aromatics reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹1,030.8 Cr (+11% YoY) and net profit of ₹3.3 Cr, recommending a final dividend of ₹0.50 per share.
Oriental Aromatics reported Q1FY27 results with 15% YoY revenue growth to ₹260 Cr and sequential margin improvement to 7.62%, while Mahad facility operates at 50-60% utilization
Oriental Aromatics entered into a strategic, technical and manufacturing arrangement with Unilever Industries.
